title: Viral protease-initiated lytic cell death as a universal antiviral mRNA therapy.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC record for PMID 42476130 (isOpenAccess=N, inEPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, no PMCID, no database cross-references; text-mined 'accessions' are only RRIDs for antibodies, cell lines and mice). Crossref record: only Elsevier subscription text-mining links, no data/code relations. HEAD requests: cell.com full text 403, sciencedirect.com 403, bioRxiv preprint full text and its supplementary PDF both 429 (blocked). bioRxiv API confirmed the matching preprint (10.1101/2025.11.14.688189, v1, 2025-11-15) and that its licence is 'cc_no' (no reuse permitted). Searched for a code repository for the generative design framework and found none.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the experiments comes from the Cell abstract and the bioRxiv preprint abstract: engineered gasdermin-D (GSDMD, a pore-forming cell-death protein) carrying viral protease cleavage motifs for hepatitis A virus 3C protease, Zika virus protease and SARS-CoV-2 main protease (NSP5/Mpro), plus a generative artificial-intelligence step that designed new NSP5 cleavage motifs that were then screened experimentally. No count of designed or tested motifs is stated in either abstract, and no methods or supplementary table could be retrieved.

a1_downloadable.note: No dataset exists to download. The paper is subscription-only (Cell/Elsevier, HTTP 403), has no PubMed Central copy, Europe PMC reports hasSuppl=N and no repository cross-references, and no GEO/SRA/BioProject/Zenodo/Dryad deposit or code repository was found. The matching bioRxiv preprint is served under a no-reuse licence and its full text and supplementary PDF were blocked (HTTP 429).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not verifiable, and almost certainly fails. The only plausible label (how strongly a given engineered cleavage motif triggers cell death or suppresses virus) lives in figure panels of wet-lab assays, so it would have to be reconstructed from plots rather than read from a column.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs would be short peptide cleavage-motif sequences inserted into GSDMD. No sequence table was obtainable; motifs are described only in the inaccessible methods/supplement.

a4_units_stated.note: Could not inspect any file. Likely readouts (percent lactate dehydrogenase release, viral titre in plaque-forming units, cell viability percent) come from several different assays, which the checklist treats as a mixed-units risk.

a5_enough_rows.note: No row count verified. A wet-lab screen of engineered gasdermin variants and designed peptide motifs is tens of sequences at most, far below the ~400 minimum for classification; neither abstract reports a number.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <1 MB if the motif table existed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem here; a peptide-motif table would be trivially small. Not verified because no file could be opened.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot compare counts: there is no download, and the paper's own counts of designed/tested motifs are not stated in any text I could retrieve.

a8_label_provenance.note: Cannot trace labels. Part of the sequence set was produced by the authors' own generative model, so any 'designed motif' records risk mixing model output with measurement; the measured antiviral readouts themselves are genuine assays but are only available as figures.

existing_models.name: ProsperousPlus (2023 web platform for protease-specific cleavage-site prediction)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported average area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC) 0.966 across proteases on MEROPS-derived independent test sets; pretrained models for 110 protease types plus a train-your-own module.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Coverage is limited to proteases with enough curated MEROPS substrates; rare or viral proteases with few known substrates remain poorly served (from the retrieved description of the platform).

existing_models.name: Procleave (2020, sequence plus structure cleavage-site predictor)
existing_models.score_and_split: Average AUC 0.950 on the same MEROPS-based benchmark, as reported in the ProsperousPlus comparison.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Needs structural context for the substrate, which is unavailable for many sites.

existing_models.name: DeepCleave (2020, convolutional network for caspase and matrix-metalloprotease substrates)
existing_models.score_and_split: Average AUC 0.923 on the MEROPS-based benchmark, per the ProsperousPlus comparison; restricted to caspases and matrix metalloproteases.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer to proteases with little training data; the authors used transfer learning precisely because per-protease data is scarce.

existing_models.name: NetCorona 1.0 / 3CLP (coronavirus main-protease cleavage-site servers used in a 2023 SARS-CoV-2 Mpro cleavage study)
existing_models.score_and_split: Used as prediction servers in a two-dimensional-electrophoresis study of Mpro cleavage; no held-out benchmark number retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Identifying the true in-cell Mpro substrate repertoire; prediction specificity for Mpro is still weak.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model with small CPU-runnable checkpoints) for short peptide motifs
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would be enough for a few hundred short peptides, but there is no labelled set to fit a head on.
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; irrelevant here because no usable data exists.

integration.partner_dataset: MEROPS peptidase database (curated protease substrate cleavage sites), joinable in principle on protease identity and the P4-P1' peptide window
integration.join_key: protease name/MEROPS identifier plus the eight-residue cleavage window
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could a model trained on curated cleavage sites rank which designed peptide motifs make a gasdermin switch fire only in virus-infected cells? — unanswerable here, because this paper contributes no retrievable measured motifs to join.

controls.positive_control: Would be the native gasdermin-D caspase-1 cleavage motif and the known hepatitis A virus 3C consensus site, which any working model must score as cleavable; cannot be used because no measurement table is available.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling and scrambled-motif sequences; not applicable without data.
controls.external_validation: MEROPS cleavage sites for coronavirus main protease would be an independent source, but there is nothing from this paper to validate.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is supportable from this paper's data, because none of it is retrievable: the only honest statement is that the experimental readouts exist solely as figures in a subscription article.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use short peptide sequences to predict how strongly a virus's protease cuts an engineered cell-death switch.
plain_idea.train_on: Would have been the engineered gasdermin-D variants and the artificial-intelligence-designed peptide motifs tested in this paper, each paired with its cell-death or antiviral readout. The number of such examples is unknown and never stated; a wet-lab screen of this kind is typically tens of sequences.
plain_idea.predict: How efficiently a given viral protease cuts a given motif, measured by the resulting lytic cell death (lactate dehydrogenase release or viability) and by the drop in virus produced. Those measurements appear only inside figure panels.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups building protease-triggered therapeutic switches would want a ranking tool so they could skip most of the wet-lab screen; even a failure would tell them that curated cleavage-site data does not transfer to engineered switch contexts.

more_or_better_data.why: No data from this paper is accessible at all, while ProsperousPlus already ships pretrained models for 110 proteases built on MEROPS-curated substrates.

confidence_score.why: Per-motif replicate measurements may exist in the figures, but nothing is extractable, so no noise estimate or calibrated uncertainty could be built.

models_beatable.why: DeepCleave (2020) and Procleave (2020) are older convolutional/structure models evaluated on MEROPS splits, but ProsperousPlus (2023) reports average AUC 0.966 and is openly runnable, so the generic cleavage-site task is well served.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: we have no training rows from this paper, so there is nothing to add to an existing baseline and no shared evaluation split.

ml_idea: The intended project was: embed short protease cleavage motifs with ESM-2 (a protein language model) and fit a small head to predict how strongly each motif activates an engineered gasdermin-D cell-death switch, so designed switches could be ranked before synthesis. It dies at the first step because this paper publishes no motif-and-readout table; the same question would have to be attacked from MEROPS plus a public protease specificity screen instead.

effort.compute_note: No estimates possible: nothing was downloaded. Compute was never the constraint; a peptide-motif table would be kilobytes.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Ask whether any machine-readable table of cleavage motifs with measured cell-death readouts is downloadable. Answer: no — subscription-only article, no PubMed Central copy, no supplement via Europe PMC, no repository deposit. That check killed it in minutes.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A1: a wet-lab therapeutics paper with no downloadable data. Cell full text and supplement are subscription-gated (HTTP 403), there is no PubMed Central copy or supplementary listing in Europe PMC, no sequence or omics deposit, and no code for the generative design step; the matching bioRxiv preprint carries a no-reuse licence and its files were blocked. Even with the supplement, the labelled set would be the few tens of engineered gasdermin variants and designed peptide motifs scored in cell-death assays, which fails A5, and the readouts live in figure panels rather than a label column (A2).
